modules.title: West Africa: Physical Setting and ECOWAS
modules.html:
Position and Extent

West Africa lies roughly between latitudes \(4^\circ\text{N}\) and \(28^\circ\text{N}\) and longitudes \(17^\circ\text{W}\) and \(16^\circ\text{E}\), bounded by the Sahara in the north and the Atlantic Ocean in the west and south. It comprises fifteen ECOWAS states, of which Nigeria is by far the largest in population.

Relief and Drainage

Broad plains and plateaux dominate: the Fouta Djallon and Guinea Highlands (source of the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers), the Jos and Bauchi Plateaux, the Air and Adamawa Highlands, the Mandara Mountains, and coastal lowlands. Major rivers are the Niger (about 4,180 km, the longest in West Africa), Senegal, Gambia, Volta and Benue.

Climate and Vegetation Belts

Belts run roughly east-west and change with distance from the coast: equatorial (Guinea) climate with rainforest on the south coast; tropical continental (Sudan) climate with savanna inland; semi-desert (Sahel); and desert (Saharan) in the far north, with a small Mediterranean margin in the extreme north-west. Rainfall is controlled by the seasonal migration of the ITD between the moist south-west monsoon and the dry north-east trades.

ECOWAS

The Economic Community of West African States was formed by the Treaty of Lagos on 28 May 1975, with headquarters in Abuja.

  • Aims: promote economic integration and trade, free movement of persons, goods and capital, harmonise agricultural and industrial policies, improve transport and telecommunications, and maintain regional peace and security.
  • Achievements: ECOWAS travel certificate and passport with visa-free movement, trade liberalisation scheme, ECOMOG peace-keeping in Liberia, Sierra Leone and The Gambia, joint road and power projects (Trans-West African Highway, West African Power Pool, West African Gas Pipeline), and cooperation in agriculture and health.
  • Problems: different colonial languages and currencies, similar (competitive rather than complementary) exports, political instability and coups, smuggling and border closures, poor transport links, and inadequate funding of the common fund.

Transport and Trade

Most railways run inland from the coast, built to export minerals and cash crops, with few east-west links; roads have therefore become the dominant mode. Major ports include Lagos (Apapa, Tin Can), Tema, Takoradi, Abidjan, Dakar and Cotonou. Intra-regional trade remains low (under 15% of total trade) because member states export similar primary goods to Europe, Asia and America.

examples.q: Give four reasons why trade among ECOWAS member states remains low.
examples.a: (i) Member states export similar primary products such as cocoa, groundnut, timber and crude oil, so their economies compete rather than complement each other; (ii) different currencies and monetary zones (CFA franc, naira, cedi) complicate payments; (iii) poor east-west transport links, since colonial railways ran inland from individual ports; (iv) language barriers between anglophone, francophone and lusophone states, plus persistent tariff barriers, smuggling and occasional border closures.

examples.q: Explain why the climatic belts of West Africa run roughly east-west.
examples.a: The controlling factor is the seasonal north-south migration of the Inter-Tropical Discontinuity, which separates the moist south-west monsoon from the dry north-east trades. Because the moist air from the Atlantic penetrates progressively less far inland, rainfall totals and length of the rainy season decrease steadily with distance north of the coast. As the region has few north-south mountain barriers, this latitudinal gradient produces belts of climate, and hence of vegetation, that are aligned east-west parallel to the coast.

modules.html:
Major Agricultural Belts

ProductLeading regionsConditions required
WheatCanadian Prairies, US Great Plains, Ukrainian and Russian Steppes, Argentine Pampas, AustraliaCool moist growing season, warm dry harvest, 380-750 mm rain, level land, chernozem soils, mechanisation
RiceMonsoon Asia - China, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Thailand, VietnamOver 1,500 mm rainfall or irrigation, temperatures above 21 C, impervious clayey soils, abundant labour
CocoaCote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Nigeria, Cameroon, Brazil, Indonesia1,000-2,000 mm well distributed rain, 21-32 C, deep well-drained forest soils, shade and shelter from wind
RubberMalaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Liberia, NigeriaHot wet equatorial climate, over 2,000 mm rain, deep soils, cheap tapping labour
CoffeeBrazil, Colombia, Ethiopia, Kenya, VietnamWarm frost-free uplands, moderate rainfall, well-drained volcanic soils
Livestock ranchingArgentine Pampas, US Great Plains, Australia, New ZealandExtensive grassland, low density of population, refrigeration and export outlets

Major Industrial Regions

  • Western Europe: Ruhr (coal, iron and steel, chemicals), Midlands and Lancashire, Northern France, Randstad.
  • North America: the Manufacturing Belt from New England through Pittsburgh and Detroit to Chicago, and California (aerospace, electronics).
  • Eastern Europe and Russia: Donetsk, Moscow, Ural and Kuznetsk regions.
  • Asia: Japan (Tokyo-Yokohama, Osaka-Kobe), China (Shanghai, Guangdong, Manchuria), India (Mumbai, Kolkata, Chota Nagpur), and the newly industrialised economies of South Korea, Taiwan and Singapore.

Common factors favouring these regions are ample power supply, iron ore and coal or imported raw materials, skilled labour, capital, large domestic markets, excellent transport (especially port facilities) and supportive government policy.

Global Trade and Groupings

Important economic groupings include ECOWAS, the African Union and AfCFTA, the European Union, OPEC, ASEAN, NAFTA/USMCA and the Commonwealth. World trade routes of note are the North Atlantic route, the Suez route linking Europe with Asia, the Panama route, and the Cape route used by very large crude carriers. Developing countries generally export primary products and import manufactured goods, which produces unfavourable terms of trade.

examples.q: State four conditions that favour cocoa cultivation in West Africa.
examples.a: (i) Heavy, well-distributed rainfall of about 1,000-2,000 mm with no long dry spell; (ii) high uniform temperatures of about 21-32 degrees Celsius with high humidity; (iii) deep, well-drained, fertile forest loams rich in humus; (iv) shelter from strong winds and shade for young plants, together with abundant cheap labour for planting, harvesting and fermenting the beans.

examples.q: Why did heavy industry develop in the Ruhr region of Germany?
examples.a: The Ruhr possessed extensive coalfields providing coking coal for smelting, with iron ore available locally at first and later imported cheaply through Rotterdam. Navigable rivers and a dense canal, rail and road network gave low-cost transport, the Rhinelands offered abundant water and skilled labour, and a huge European market lay close by. Government support and reinvested capital reinforced these advantages, making the region a centre for iron and steel, chemicals and engineering.

quiz.solution: The Treaty of Lagos was signed on 28 May 1975.

quiz.q: The headquarters of ECOWAS is located in
quiz.solution: The ECOWAS Commission has its headquarters in Abuja, Nigeria.

quiz.q: The longest river in West Africa is the
quiz.solution: The Niger is about 4,180 km long.

quiz.q: The Fouta Djallon Highlands are important because they
options: are the source of major rivers
quiz.solution: The Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers rise there.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT an aim of ECOWAS?
quiz.solution: ECOWAS promotes cooperation among sovereign states, not colonisation.

quiz.q: A major obstacle to ECOWAS integration is
options: a common currency for all members
similar competitive exports and different currencies
quiz.solution: Member economies compete rather than complement one another.

quiz.q: Climatic belts in West Africa run roughly
quiz.solution: They follow latitude because of the north-south migration of the ITD.

quiz.q: The peace-keeping arm of ECOWAS is known as
quiz.solution: ECOMOG intervened in Liberia, Sierra Leone and The Gambia.

quiz.q: Wheat cultivation on the Canadian Prairies is favoured by
options: level land, chernozem soils and mechanisation
quiz.solution: Extensive level land allows large-scale mechanised farming on fertile black earths.

quiz.q: Rice production is concentrated in monsoon Asia mainly because of
options: heavy rainfall, clayey soils and abundant labour
quiz.solution: Padi rice needs standing water on impervious soils and much hand labour.

quiz.q: The world's leading producer of cocoa is
quiz.solution: Cote d'Ivoire has been the leading cocoa producer for decades.

quiz.q: Natural rubber is produced mainly in
quiz.solution: Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand dominate world natural rubber output.

quiz.q: The Ruhr industrial region owes its growth mainly to
options: coal and good transport by river and canal
quiz.solution: Coking coal, cheap water transport and a large market attracted heavy industry.

quiz.q: Which of these organisations is concerned with petroleum exports?
quiz.solution: OPEC coordinates petroleum policies of major oil exporting countries.

quiz.q: Developing countries generally suffer unfavourable terms of trade because they
options: export primary products and import manufactures
quiz.solution: Primary product prices fluctuate and rise more slowly than those of manufactures.

quiz.q: The Suez Canal is important because it shortens the route between
quiz.solution: It avoids the long voyage round the Cape of Good Hope.

quiz.q: Most railways in West Africa run inland from the coast because they were built to
options: evacuate minerals and cash crops for export
quiz.solution: Colonial lines were designed to move raw materials to the ports.
